answer: An agent identity requires a stake bond deposited with a registration cipher and a one-per-hardware attestation signed by the device vendor. Registration locks 500 units, a confirmed duplicate slashes the full bond after a 30-epoch challenge window, and the vendor credential revokes at once. Each additional fake identity costs another full bond and a distinct device, so marginal cost stays flat while a shared crystal or juniper key exposes every linked identity to one slashing event.
